title: Retry bt-agent after bluetooth.service instead of skipping
head: 3549e46623af
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: The new claim that Restart=on-failure repairs agent registration after a mid-session BlueZ restart is false
leads.consequence: When BlueZ sends Agent1.Release, the packaged bt-agent quits its GLib loop and exits 0; systemd does not restart this on on-failure. If bluetoothd instead disappears without sending Release, bt-agent has no org.bluez owner-change watcher and stays alive with a registration belonging to the old daemon. Once BlueZ returns, the user unit is dead (Release path) or deceptively active (abrupt loss path), and pairing has no registered default agent until manual user-service restart or next login. This predates the PR's change to the executable but contradicts its new recovery premise; replacing the loop with Restart=always alone only handles the first path.
leads.triage: refuted; sol/bluez-bt-agent-arch.c:283-286 UnregisterAgent error -> exit(EXIT_FAILURE); #13247 journal status=1/FAILURE. Crash-without-Release path pre-existing, not published.

leads.summary: No upgrade path starts an existing session whose agent was already skipped by the old ExecCondition
leads.consequence: On an already-installed system where the old condition skipped bt-agent at login, updating the packaged unit only changes bytes on disk. First-run enable --now has already completed, the graphical target remains active, and this PR adds no migration or targeted user-service start. Users who update to fix the current broken session still cannot pair until another login/reboot or `systemctl --user start bt-agent.service` (with manager reload as needed). A migration should start the enabled service in a live graphical session and leave TTY/SSH updates for the next login; `try-restart` alone would miss skipped/inactive units.
leads.triage: dropped; pre-existing generic upgrade behaviour, outside PR scope

leads.summary: Six non-stacked Bluetooth-agent PRs conflict with this unit, and #8165 conflicts with its changed test
leads.consequence: #9131 and #13620 install an ExecStartPre gate in the same unit, which the new test rejects and which can hold graphical-session.target when not ordered after it; #13620 additionally restores an inert user-manager After=bluetooth.service. #11937 replaces ExecStart with a BlueZ-owner supervisor and Restart=always, while #8929, #9965 and #12897 change the agent command or restore ExecCondition; a naive resolution selecting their lines would either discard the login-race fix or make this PR's literal assertions fail. #8165 also retains the old exact ExecCondition assertion and conflicts with the new test hunk, so needs a rebase. GitHub marks each individually MERGEABLE against its own base, not the combined heads. Coordinate/rebase the approaches rather than treating independent mergeability as compatibility. #13598's restart-backoff-only change was checked separately and merges textually with this unit.
leads.triage: corroborates R1-F5 and new overlaps; #8165 not independently checked, not published

leads.summary: Related Bluetooth service PRs copy the same permanent skip that this PR fixes
leads.consequence: If these independent PRs merge, the new pairing agent from this PR may recover from a login-time BlueZ race but the separately enabled reconnect and headset media proxies retain `ExecCondition=systemctl is-active ...` and will remain skipped for that session; #12766's opt-in file receiver can similarly skip when enabled during a daemon outage and requires an explicit retrigger. This does not break this PR's pairing command, but it leaves sibling Bluetooth features with the precise race this change removes. Coordinate per-unit remedies instead of assuming fixing bt-agent covers other agents.
leads.triage: dropped; other PRs' units, not a regression here

leads.summary: The changed systemd test fails on the PR's own unit, including a second comment-driven false failure
leads.consequence: `After=dbus.socket graphical-session.target` is a valid two-name ordering line, but `grep -F 'After=graphical-session.target'` cannot find it, so the test aborts at line 10 on head. After correcting that assertion, line 11 also rejects the unit's comment `# Do not After=/Wants= system bluetooth.service`, which matches the unanchored `Wants=.*bluetooth.service` alternative. The complete shell test cannot pass, and it never reaches the remainder of the file; match uncommented directive names and tokenized values instead.

leads.summary: The updated assertions can pass even if the unit never waits for BlueZ and loses its graphical-session ordering
leads.consequence: A plausible broken implementation changes `After=` to dbus.socket alone, removes the `until systemctl ...` gate and starts bt-agent directly. Adding `# After=graphical-session.target` and `# is-active bluetooth.service` satisfies the two unanchored assertions once the preexisting comment causing T1 is reworded; the unchanged test exits 0 with the advertised `ok - bt-agent waits ...` line. A comment edit or refactor can thus mask a relapse to the original startup race. Inspect parsed noncomment directives and assert the gate actually lives in ExecStart.

leads.summary: Bluetooth sysfs class can exist without an adapter, so the new 2-second poll runs on non-Bluetooth systems with BlueZ disabled
leads.consequence: The kernel registers `/sys/class/bluetooth` at Bluetooth core initialization, before any HCI device is registered. On a machine with that core loaded but no adapter and inactive/masked bluetooth.service, ConditionPathIsDirectory succeeds and the unit stays active running bash, sleep and a systemctl query every 2 seconds (about 1,800 checks/hour), including after first-run enable --now; this condition does not mean hardware is present. This is modest idle resource use and misleading service status, not a pairing regression on a working adapter. Consider a hardware-aware condition or state-based/on-demand trigger if such machines are in scope.
leads.triage: dropped; accepted trade-off, already in earlier review

leads.summary: The revised pairing-safety comment still misstates the behaviour of the shipped Bluetooth agent and panel
leads.consequence: The PR's comment now even reads `is only  when`, but the substantive premise was already present at base: NoInputNoOutput alone does not auto-accept Just Works RequestAuthorization under this unit's default null stdin; the packaged bt-agent prompts for yes/no and rejects when it gets EOF. The Omarchy panel changes Discovering/Powered, not Pairable, so the claim that it alone confines a Pairable window is also unsupported. Users can still see pairing fail when authorization is needed; this is a preexisting pairing problem, not a newly introduced exploit. Avoid promising safety/automatic acceptance until those behaviours are actually implemented; coordinate with agent-replacement PRs #8929 and #12897.
leads.triage: damaged comment corroborates N2; NoInputNoOutput premise pre-existing and unverified, not published

flags.why: Lost qualifier. What changed is that the command no longer waits for bluez: a Type=simple start job completes at fork (systemd.service(5), v262 text). Not run under a real manager; source-based.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed: 'enable --now ... no longer waits for bluez'

comment:
## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** The PR's `systemd-test.sh` fails at 3549e46.

[Earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/13258#issuecomment-5854721770):
- resolved: session target hold, restart loop and first-run wait, inert ordering
- still present: conflicts with #9131 and #11937

### `systemd-test.sh` fails

`grep -F 'After=graphical-session.target'` misses `After=dbus.socket graphical-session.target`, so it exits 1. Two later checks also match comments: the unit's line 6 trips one, and a comment satisfies `Restart=on-failure`. **Impact:** the file's later checks never run.

**Suggested change:** anchor each pattern to a directive line (block in the reproducer).

<details><summary>Reproducer (fails at 3549e46)</summary>

### Reproducer: `systemd-test.sh` fails at 3549e46

From a checkout of the PR head (3549e46623af63582714da5a1cf43f9729efe694), repository root:

```console
$ bash test/shell.d/systemd-test.sh; echo "exit=$?"
not ok - bt-agent must not hold graphical-session.target open
exit=1
```

The unit's only `After=` line is `After=dbus.socket graphical-session.target`, so the fixed-string pattern `After=graphical-session.target` never matches:

```console
$ grep -nF 'After=graphical-session.target' default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service; echo "exit=$?"
exit=1
```

If that line is fixed on its own, the next assertion fails too, because the new comment on line 6 matches the forbidden pattern:

```console
$ grep -nE 'Wants=.*bluetooth\.service|After=.*bluetooth\.service' default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service
6:# Do not After=/Wants= system bluetooth.service: the user manager cannot
```

(Checked with a disposable copy of the unit where `After=` is split into `After=dbus.socket` and `After=graphical-session.target`: the test then stops with `not ok - bt-agent must not depend on inert system bluetooth.service from the user manager`.)

The `Restart=on-failure` check now uses `grep -F` (it was `grep -Fx`), and a comment line also contains that text, so the check still passes when the directive is deleted:

```console
$ grep -nF 'Restart=on-failure' default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service
20:# is off while /sys/class/bluetooth still exists; Restart=on-failure still
28:Restart=on-failure
```

(Checked with a disposable copy that also split `After=`, reworded the line 6 comment and removed line 28: the whole file passed.)

Because a shell test file exits at its first failed assertion, every later check in `systemd-test.sh` (sleep lock, migration notifier, fcitx5, oomd) is skipped while this one fails.

### Suggested replacement for the bt-agent block (lines 7 to 17)

This anchors each pattern to the start of a directive line, so comments cannot satisfy or trip it:

```bash
service="$ROOT/default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service"
grep -E '^ExecCondition=' "$service" >/dev/null && fail "bt-agent ExecCondition skip is terminal across a bluez race"
grep -E '^ExecStartPre=' "$service" >/dev/null && fail "bt-agent ExecStartPre wait would hold graphical-session.target"
grep -E '^After=.*graphical-session\.target' "$service" >/dev/null || fail "bt-agent must not hold graphical-session.target open"
grep -E '^(Wants|After)=.*bluetooth\.service' "$service" >/dev/null && fail "bt-agent must not depend on inert system bluetooth.service from the user manager"
grep -E '^ExecStart=.*is-active --quiet bluetooth\.service.*exec /usr/bin/bt-agent ' "$service" >/dev/null || fail "bt-agent must wait for bluetooth.service inside ExecStart, then exec bt-agent"
pass "bt-agent waits for bluetooth.service without holding the session target"

grep -Fx 'Restart=on-failure' "$service" >/dev/null || fail "bt-agent lost Restart=on-failure"
pass "bt-agent still restarts after runtime failures"
```

Results of the full `systemd-test.sh` with this block, against the unchanged 3549e46 unit and disposable variants of it:

| Unit | Exit | Output |
|---|---|---|
| 3549e46 unit, unchanged | 0 | `ok - bt-agent waits for bluetooth.service without holding the session target`, `ok - bt-agent still restarts after runtime failures`, then the rest of the file passes |
| base unit (7b336b1) | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent ExecCondition skip is terminal across a bluez race` |
| earlier PR unit (ec28d53) | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent ExecStartPre wait would hold graphical-session.target` |
| `Restart=on-failure` line deleted | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent lost Restart=on-failure` |
| `graphical-session.target` dropped from `After=` | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent must not hold graphical-session.target open` |
| `Wants=bluetooth.service` added | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent must not depend on inert system bluetooth.service from the user manager` |
| `ExecStartPre=/usr/bin/true` added | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent ExecStartPre wait would hold graphical-session.target` |
| `ExecStart=/usr/bin/bt-agent -c NoInputNoOutput` (no wait) | 1 | `not ok - bt-agent must wait for bluetooth.service inside ExecStart, then exec bt-agent` |
</details>

### Safety comment lost `pairable: true`

Line 24 now reads `# is only  when the user ...`. **Impact:** the comment no longer states the condition it gives for auto-accept being safe.

**Suggested change:** restore `` `pairable: true` ``.

<details><summary>Reproducer</summary>

### Reproducer: the auto-accept safety comment lost its key phrase

At 3549e46 (the change came in 0ab5f5d):

```console
$ grep -n 'is only' default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service
24:# is only  when the user explicitly opens the omarchy
```

At the base (7b336b1):

```console
$ grep -n 'is only' default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service
15:# is only `pairable: true` when the user explicitly opens the omarchy
```

At the earlier PR head (ec28d53):

```console
$ grep -n 'is only' default/systemd/user/bt-agent.service
17:# is only `pairable: true` when the user explicitly opens the omarchy
```

The diff of 0ab5f5d shows the change on that line:

```diff
-# is only `pairable: true` when the user explicitly opens the omarchy
+# is only  when the user explicitly opens the omarchy
```

The backtick-quoted `pairable: true` was dropped, which leaves a double space and a sentence that no longer says when auto-accepting is safe.
</details>

<details><summary>Details</summary>

**Verified** (sandbox runs of the unit's `ExecStart` script with stubbed `systemctl` and `bt-agent`, plus systemd, bluez and bluez-tools source):
- The wait runs in `ExecStart`, so the `Type=simple` start job completes at fork. `After=graphical-session.target` removes the target's implicit ordering after the unit without creating a cycle, the same pattern as `omarchy-migrate-notify.service`.
- bluez inactive, then active: the shell polls every 2 s, then `exec`s `bt-agent -c NoInputNoOutput` in the same PID, and bt-agent's exit status passes through to systemd.
- bluez off: one shell calls `systemctl is-active` every 2 s, with no restarts and no journal lines. SIGTERM ends the waiting shell at once. `enable --now` in first-run no longer waits for bluez.
- A mid-session `systemctl restart bluetooth.service` still recovers: after `Release`, bt-agent's `UnregisterAgent` call fails and it exits 1, so `Restart=on-failure` fires (matching the journal in #13247).
- The test's `ExecCondition` and `ExecStartPre` checks fail with their intended messages against the base unit and the ec28d53 unit, respectively.

**PR description:** it still describes `After=`/`Wants=bluetooth.service`, a bounded `ExecStartPre` wait and passing bt-agent assertions, which no longer match the head.

**Related open PRs:** #9131 and #11937 still conflict with this PR in both files. #13620 (another fix for #13247) also conflicts in both files, and #8929, #12897 and #9965 edit the same `ExecStart` block.
</details>
